correctness.rationale: The two maximum labels must be adjacent, so inserting the new largest pair in all gaps gives the complete source and target families with counts 945 and 105. Nested matching-label intervals give an independent enumeration as preorder-labelled plane forests below a root, with labels increasing along paths. Erasing a label removes that node while splicing its ordered children into its old place; relabelling the survivors by increasing rank gives the required standardized output, whether the erased node is a leaf or not. All possible outputs for each source were independently formed and deduplicated. The certificate's 33 indices have disjoint shadows using 104 different targets. Its 105 nonnegative integer weights sum to 339636, and all 945 distinct-target sums are at least 10000. Thus any code uses weight at least 10000 per source without double counting a target, and 34 sources would require at least 340000. The exact optimum is 33 without any optimality assumption about the certificate's search method.
residual_risks: The exhaustive check is for order five only. The receiver obtains one standardized descendant, not the deck, erasure locations or the erased label.

value.rationale: The question is an exact zero-error capacity for natural labelled tree descriptions under a single unknown contraction. It is a genuine finite packing problem across 945 sources, not a trivial consequence of output-space size or the sizes of individual shadows. The witnesses give a near-cover of the available smaller trees and a strict upper threshold, answering exactly how many distinct five-edge structures can be encoded against this deletion. The finite answer is usable as a benchmark or base case without claiming a general-order theorem.
residual_risks: Value is for the precise constrained five-label channel; no arbitrary-order capacity, general construction, or robustness to other deletions is established.
